stem: Best guess: which shareholder would make a corporation ineligible for S status?

choices.explanation: Individuals who are citizens are eligible.
Correct. Partnerships, C corporations, and nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

explanation: Partnerships, C corporations, and nonresident aliens are ineligible shareholders.

stem: A calendar-year corporation eligible all year files Form 2553 on March 10, 2025 with all shareholders' consent. When is the S election effective?

choices.explanation: It was filed in time for 2025.
Elections are effective at the start of a tax year.
Timely elections are effective by rule.

explanation: An election made by the 15th day of the 3rd month is effective for the current year.

stem: An S corporation with no accumulated E&P distributes $40,000 to a shareholder whose stock basis (after the year's income) is $30,000. What does the shareholder recognize?

choices.explanation: The excess over basis is gain.
Correct. Tax-free up to basis (30,000); excess 10,000 is capital gain.

explanation: Tax-free up to basis (30,000); excess 10,000 is capital gain.

stem: Which feature would create a second class of stock and terminate S status?

choices.text: Voting and nonvoting common stock with identical distribution rights

choices.explanation: Correct. Differences in distribution or liquidation rights create a second class of stock.

choices.text: A shareholder that is an estate

explanation: Differences in distribution or liquidation rights create a second class of stock.

stem: A shareholder guarantees a $100,000 bank loan to her S corporation. What effect does the guarantee have on her basis?

choices.text: Basis increases by her ownership percentage of the loan

choices.explanation: A guarantee doesn't increase stock basis.

choices.text: No effect unless she actually pays on the guarantee
choices.explanation: Correct. S corporation debt basis requires a direct loan from the shareholder (unlike partnership liability sharing).

explanation: S corporation debt basis requires a direct loan from the shareholder (unlike partnership liability sharing).

stem: A former C corporation converted to S status in 2022 and sells an asset in 2025 that had a $50,000 built-in gain at conversion. What entity-level tax applies?
explanation: §1374: 21% on net recognized built-in gain within 5 years after conversion (the gain also passes through, reduced by the tax).

stem: An S corporation shareholder's stock basis is $20,000 at the start of 2025. Her share of ordinary income is $35,000 and of tax-exempt interest $2,000; she receives a $30,000 distribution. What is her ending stock basis?

choices.explanation: Omits tax-exempt income and the distribution.

explanation: Income items (including tax-exempt) increase basis before distributions reduce it.

stem: An S corporation with accumulated E&P of $15,000 and an AAA of $10,000 distributes $30,000 to its sole shareholder (stock basis $50,000). How is it treated?

choices.text: $10,000 tax-free (AAA), $15,000 dividend, $5,000 tax-free return of basis
choices.explanation: Correct. Ordering: AAA → accumulated E&P → remaining basis → gain.

explanation: Ordering: AAA → accumulated E&P → remaining basis → gain.

stem: How are an S corporation's items allocated when a shareholder sells stock mid-year (no election to close the books)?

choices.text: According to who owned stock at year-end
choices.explanation: Allocation is per share per day.

choices.text: Pro rata per share, per day

choices.explanation: S corporations allocate by shares and days.

stem: A 100% shareholder-employee of an S corporation takes no salary, only distributions. What is the IRS's likely position?

choices.text: Part of the distributions should be recharacterized as wages subject to payroll taxes
choices.explanation: Correct. Shareholder-employees must receive reasonable compensation for services.
Low salary doesn't terminate the election.
Dividend treatment isn't the issue here.

explanation: Shareholder-employees must receive reasonable compensation for services.

stem: An S corporation's election terminated in 2025. Absent IRS consent, when can it re-elect S status?

choices.explanation: Correct. §1362(g): a 5-year wait after termination unless the IRS consents.
It can re-elect after the waiting period.

explanation: §1362(g): a 5-year wait after termination unless the IRS consents.

stem: A 50% shareholder has stock basis of $8,000 and a $5,000 direct loan to the S corporation. Her share of the ordinary loss is $20,000. How much can she deduct?
explanation: Losses are deductible up to stock basis plus debt basis; the remaining 7,000 is suspended.

stem: When is Form 1120-S due for a calendar-year S corporation?

choices.explanation: Correct. S corporations file by the 15th day of the 3rd month.
That's the C corporation due date.
That's the extended C corporation date.

explanation: S corporations file by the 15th day of the 3rd month.
